newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Israel housing not conducive to trust.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Israel housing not conducive to trust.

text.p: A U.S. official, speaking shortly before Israel approved new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem on Wednesday, suggested such a move would not be conducive to building trust in the Middle East.
"Since the Hebron agreement we have encouraged all of the parties to take actions which build confidence and trust," White House spokesman David Johnson told reporters.
"The reports about decisions which may be made are not the type of actions we would believe would help build that."
Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told reporters on Wednesday a ministerial committee on Jerusalem had approved building new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.
Naveh said that the committee approved the construction of 6,500 homes for Jews, with 2,500 to be build in the first stage. Another 3,000 housing units would be build for Arabs.
A U.S. official contacted after Naveh's announcement said he could not go beyond Johnson's earlier remarks.
Earlier this year the United States helped to broker an accord between Israel and the Palestianians on a much-delayed partial Israeli troop withdrawal from the West Bank city of Hebron.
